analysis: Reviewed the supplied units of provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/KVCacheSSD/SSDPrefixCacheTests.swift. The change is test-only. Head ranges 3140-3240 add two tests, remembersHeaderVerdictsOnlyForUnchangedFiles and replacedLookalikeIsReadAgain. They exercise SSDWholeRootMaintainer.shared.maintain. The first test checks that a cached header-ownership verdict is not reused after a same-size, mtime-restored overwrite (detected via ctime). The second checks that a malformed lookalike later replaced by a real block is re-read and owned. These tests support the T-041 mitigations on TTL/LRU sweeping and on not deleting or owning non-Darkbloom files. I saw no production source change in this batch, so no new attack surface and no weakening of controls (HMAC names, DBK3 AAD, TTL, KEK purge, symlink no-follow). The supplied units are base lines 4238-4588 and head lines 1-609, which are mostly unchanged context. The head excerpt does not reach the added tests at 3140-3240, and the patch excerpt is truncated. The production change that the tests imply (a verdict cache keyed on file identity, size, mtime and ctime in SSDWholeRootMaintainer) is not supplied, so I could not verify it. Integration should check that source if present: the cache key must include inode, size, mtime and ctime. Eviction must still be restricted to verified owned files, and stale verdicts must not allow deleting non-owned files or skipping TTL expiry. This is an unverified contract, not a finding.
